name: Project MOE
description: MOE is ERPL's flagship liquid bipropellant launch vehicle, designed for a 60,000-foot flight at approximately Mach 2.5. The program integrates a 2,250 lbf engine, cryogenic feed system, avionics, structures, and recovery hardware.

details.about: MOE is a LOX/IPA liquid bipropellant rocket designed to reach approximately 60,000 feet. Building on the experience gained from Odyssey, Juno, and Triton, the team is conducting integrated testing and preparing the vehicle for the Friends of Amateur Rocketry Dollar-Per-Foot Challenge.

name: Fluids
description: Fluids owns ERPL's high-pressure and cryogenic feed systems, from P&IDs and component sizing through assembly and test. The division operates Draco and develops the MOE flight feed system.

details.about: Fluids designs, integrates, and operates ERPL's propellant feed systems, pressurization systems, and ground support equipment. Its members size components, produce system layouts, assemble hardware, and run supervised cryogenic and high-pressure operations on Draco and MOE.

newMembers.summary: New members start on real feed-system hardware with experienced review and supervised testing.
work: Read P&IDs and work through pressure drop, orifice, and relief sizing.
CAD tank restraints, brackets, and fluid-system layouts.
Assemble hardware and support supervised leak, water, and pressure tests.

name: Electronics
description: Electronics commands, controls, and instruments ERPL's propulsion systems. The division builds the circuitry, software, sensor interfaces, and data systems used from bench checkout through remote test operations.

details.about: Electronics develops ERPL's control systems, data acquisition hardware, engine control units, sensor interfaces, data logging, and ground station software. Members carry hardware and software from bench validation to remote operation and data collection during tests.

newMembers.summary: New members take a channel or subsystem from bench checkout to live test support.
work: Build and inspect cable harnesses, sensor interfaces, and circuit boards.
Calibrate pressure transducers, load cells, and thermocouples.
Write embedded or ground software and support supervised test operations.

name: Structures & Dynamics
description: Structures & Dynamics develops MOE's airframe, aerodynamics, recovery systems, and flight simulation. The division carries analysis into fabrication, inspection, and ground testing.

details.about: Structures & Dynamics owns vehicle aerodynamics, primary structures, recovery systems, and flight simulation. Lessons from Spectre, ERPL's actively stabilized rocket, now inform the MOE airframe and flight systems.

newMembers.summary: New members own bounded flight-hardware problems and carry them through analysis and test.
work: CAD airframe, recovery, and test-fixture components.
Run hand calculations, aerodynamic models, and structural analysis.
Fabricate, inspect, and ground-test composite and metallic hardware.

name: Engines
description: Engines takes ERPL propulsion systems from cycle calculations and injector design through integration, instrumentation, hot fire, and post-test analysis.

details.about: Engines owns propulsion design, integration, test support, and data reduction. The program has progressed from the Odyssey hybrid to the Juno and Triton liquid engines, with MOE combining those lessons at flight scale.

newMembers.summary: New members begin with a defined engine problem, not a semester of observation.
work: Calculate mass flow, injector sizing, nozzle performance, and thermal loads.
CAD injector and thrust-chamber components for design review.
Support engine assembly and instrumentation, then reduce hot-fire data.

name: Triton
description: Triton is a LOX/ethanol engine in the 1,000 lbf class. Designed and built by first-year members, it completed two successful hot-fire tests at Cecil Spaceport in spring 2025.

details.about: Triton represents a significant step up in engine capability from Juno. The first engine at ERPL designed and built by first-year members, Triton moved from initial training to two successful hot fires in ten months and remains a testbed for future component designs.

name: Juno
description: Juno returned ERPL to cryogenic liquid bipropellant engine development. Its adjustable operating point supported early work in LOX handling, injector design, and ignition systems.

details.about: Juno was ERPL's first liquid bipropellant engine program in more than a decade. Designed for short-duration LOX/ethanol tests across a range of operating conditions, its feed, injector, and igniter work informed Triton and MOE.

name: Odyssey
description: Odyssey was a 500 lbf nominal HTPB/nitrous oxide hybrid engine that reached approximately 600 lbf at peak. Its campaign rebuilt ERPL's experience in feed systems, data acquisition, and test operations.

details.about: Project Odyssey was a 500 lbf nominal hybrid rocket engine utilizing HTPB and nitrous oxide as propellants. It reached approximately 600 lbf at peak and was fired twice, with the second test ending in thermal failure. The campaign established propellant feed infrastructure, custom data collection, and the operating procedures used by later engines. Odyssey is retired and on display in the College of Engineering.
